name: Corselette

card.summary: A one-piece foundation garment combining bra and girdle that supports the bust and smooths the waist and hips for a shaped silhouette.
card.aka: Corselet, all-in-one, panty corselette, Merry Widow

quick.overview:
A corselette is a women's foundation garment that joins a bra and a girdle in one piece, with shoulder straps and a body extending to the top of the thighs. It lifts the bust and smooths the torso under clothes.
It became popular in 1914 as an alternative to wearing a bra with a girdle or corset, and styles include open versions with suspenders and panty versions. Its shaping lasts only while worn.
quick.how: It is worn under clothing in place of a separate bra and girdle. Boning or wires support the cups and keep strapless versions in place; some designs use panels of non-stretch fabric through the front to flatten and shape.
quick.risks: No specific risks are documented beyond general discomfort associated with compressive garments.

lead: A corselette is a women's foundation garment combining a bra and a girdle, with shoulder straps and a body that extends down to around the top of the legs; it can include lace and be open-style with suspenders or panty-style [1].

It supports the bust and controls the waist and hips so that clothing sits smoothly. A Chinese utility model patent for a siamesed panty-corselette describes design aims of supporting the chest and thinning the waist, using a non-stretch central panel [2].

chain: Girdle section compresses waist and hips
Smoother, more defined silhouette while worn
angle.text: The garment shapes the body under clothes by lifting the bust and compressing the midsection. The effect lasts only while it is worn.

paras: The word likely derives from corset plus the diminutive -ette; the older corselet named a piece of plate armor [1]. The corselette became popular in 1914 as a single-piece alternative to a separate bra and girdle or corset [1]. Bust uplift cups appeared in 1933 but became common from 1943, and in 1952 Warner's released the Merry Widow, which used elastic netting, a zipper and nine spiral wires [1]. From around 1960, tights and trousers began replacing corselettes [1].

Boning supports the cup section and helps strapless versions stay up [1]. Modern designs, such as the patented siamesed panty-corselette, combine a front panel, back panel, legs and shoulder straps with a central non-stretch zone intended to support the chest and thin the waist [2].

timeline.event: Corselettes become popular as a one-piece alternative to bra plus girdle [1].
Tights and trousers begin replacing corselettes [1].
